plan_ref.note: A plain path with the revision in `rev`, per R13: the '@r<N>' form inside a ref string is what r3 and r7 carry, and it bypasses R6's revision branch. Those two keep their warnings -- they are sealed and cited, and a warning standing on a document that predates a field is the only record of when the vocabulary changed.

claim: P7's blocker was misnamed. It is not a data transfer: the tracked positions can be read where they are, by a tool that runs anywhere, so what the precondition waits on is a person choosing either of two interchangeable actions. `needs_data_transfer` states a requirement the design does not have, and a reader planning the next round around it would plan for the wrong thing.

answering_quantity.why: This document asks for nothing. It corrects one field of r7, which this side wrote, and r8 has already answered r7's actual question. Following r4's precedent deliberately: folding a new ask into a correction lets the correction be read as a negotiation, so the next question travels separately.

required_precision.basis: Structurally required by the schema and carrying no meaning here, because nothing is being asked. The value 1 is a placeholder and is not a target; no simulator time should be spent against it.

what_would_change_my_mind: Nothing, in the sense a claim usually means: this is a correction to a field of this side's own document rather than a hypothesis about the world. If the tracked positions turn out to be unreadable where they are -- a format no numpy reader can open, or a machine nobody can run a Python process on -- then `needs_data_transfer` was right after all and this correction is itself wrong. Neither is true today: the files are two columns of text and the fit needs three packages.

system_primitives.source: data/particles.yaml bangs-dragongreen-5um-cooh, measured lot mean. Unchanged across r1, r3, r7 -- carried because the schema requires at least one primitive and this document introduces none.

corrects.what: gaps[0].kind, on the gap 'The per-rung scatter on the drag-slope gamma, measured on real data'.
corrects.why: The field named a requirement the design does not have. `drag-prepare` and `drag-slope` read a path and know nothing about a microscope: numpy, pyyaml and pytest are the whole dependency list, so the fit runs wherever the file already is. Moving the bytes is therefore one of two interchangeable conveniences and not a precondition -- and the files are kilobytes, two columns and one row per frame, so neither option is even costly. The operator settled it the same way on 2026-09-16: producing a plan does not require being on site.

am:kb/plans/2026-09-15-drag-calibration-stiffness-vs-size.md#P7 -- already corrected, at rev 4c52c4e: 'blocked on a person doing one of two interchangeable things', with the procedure expanded into four steps and the preparation step named.

gaps.what: The per-rung scatter on the drag-slope gamma, on real data.
gaps.why: The tracked positions of the 2026-09-03 run have not been identified yet -- specifically the ones from BEFORE `creepx`, which detrends the mean displacement away by design, so its output cannot be used however it is post-processed.
gaps.consequence: The number that gets compared against r8's 4.48 % does not exist yet, so nothing in the thread has yet measured what this instrument delivers. r8's 7.2-9.5 % is a simulation of it.
gaps.would_need: A person doing either of two interchangeable things: run `python -m calibration.cli drag-prepare <files> --frame-period-ms <achieved> --frame-period-source <where from>` then `drag-slope` where the files are, or copy them first and run the same two commands here. The design does not care which. What it does care about is the frame period: these files carry no time column, and the analysis PC hardcodes 0.02 s without reading metadata, so the period has to come from a timestamp column or a run report's achieved rate.

gaps.what: A wall, and therefore h0 as a physical measurement.
gaps.why: Not a missing runner. At fixed h the wall's only effect is a scalar gamma, which enters no dimensionless group a trapped-bead case carries, so no runner can learn it. r8's gaps[0] states the same conclusion from that side.
gaps.consequence: h0 comes from this instrument or from nowhere, and r1's falsifier has fired against the ladder route on simulated evidence.
gaps.would_need: Nothing buildable. The alternative method -- testing the fit procedure on a synthetic gamma(h) -- is what r7 asked for and r8 delivered as sigma_gamma_max = 4.48 %.

out_of_scope: Any new question. r8 answered r7, and the next ask travels as its own round rather than riding on a correction -- r4 set that precedent from the other side and gave the reason: a correction that also negotiates can be read as negotiating.
r8's gaps[2], whether the ladder's six heights are the right six. Worth asking and not asked here.
Any gate threshold. 4.48 % is `simulated` and lands with may_be_gate_threshold: false; it is a design target, and nothing in trapping/ has been changed to know about it.
